contracts.commit_point: ADK tool dispatch of the execute_sql call immediately after forbidden_dml_check returns None (agent.py:89); the blocking non-None return at agent.py:86 prevents the SQL from reaching BigQuery execution. The framework-internal execution point itself is not shown in the supplied source.
contracts.declared_mechanism: forbidden_dml_check (agent.py:74-89) registered as before_tool_callback on bq_investigation_agent (agent.py:156) and decision_agent (agent.py:222); the callback returns a non-None dict (agent.py:86) to block the tool call and returns None (agent.py:89) to permit execution.
contracts.forbidden_condition: A tool call named 'execute_sql' whose 'query' argument contains any of the whole-word keywords UPDATE, DELETE, MERGE, or TRUNCATE (checked after uppercase normalization via word-boundary regex) reaching tool dispatch.

contracts.protected_operation: Execution of SQL via the execute_sql tool of the BigQueryToolset invoked by an agent during its tool-calling loop.
contracts.protected_resource: BigQuery data reachable through the shared BigQueryToolset (configured project PROJECT_ID / dataset DATASET_ID, agent.py:28-30; the instruction-level restriction 'NEVER, EVER DELETE OR MODIFY ANY EXISTING DATA IN BIGQUERY' at agent.py:152 is advisory prompt text, not the enforced mechanism).
contracts.protection_obligation: Destructive DML statements (UPDATE, DELETE, MERGE, TRUNCATE) must not be executed against BigQuery through the execute_sql tool of the shared BigQueryToolset; the forbidden_dml_check before_tool_callback must intercept such tool calls on both agents holding the toolset (bq_investigation_agent and decision_agent) and return a blocking result before the SQL is dispatched for execution. (Merges the duplicate first-phase and second-phase reviewer obligations, which name the same guard, operations, and commit point.)
scope_limits: The guard triggers only for tool calls whose tool.name is 'execute_sql' (agent.py:79); other BigQueryToolset tools are not name-checked by this callback.
Only the 'query' argument is inspected (agent.py:81); if it is absent or falsy, the keyword check is silently skipped.

Keyword matching uses a word-boundary regex over the uppercased query text (agent.py:84-85), so DML keywords anywhere in the query — including inside string literals or comments — trigger blocking; no obfuscation handling beyond .upper().strip() is declared.
The callback is registered only on bq_investigation_agent and decision_agent; the supplied source shows no before_tool_callback on google_search_agent, the orchestrator agents, or the App.

Blocking behavior relies on ADK before_tool_callback semantics (non-None return short-circuits execution), which is declared by the return value at agent.py:86 but whose enforcement is implemented outside the supplied source.
